title: $200 in one week
target_customer: Buyers with an existing broken workflow and a small paid scope
search_scope: Public buyer posts checked 20 September 2026; Portugal-based delivery; PayPal required. Quotes below are proposed prices, not advertised rewards.
verdict: Direct paid repairs are the strongest route to try. Aim for two $125 jobs or one $250 job, before fees and any taxes. No buyer has agreed to hire or pay yet. No opportunity here has confirmed PayPal terms. Earned: $0.

prospects.name: Dorian56 — stuck automation workflow
prospects.pain_signal: Posted on 18 September that an urgent workflow is stuck and explicitly offered to pay for help.
prospects.evidence: The original buyer post requests replies or DMs. The n8n public topic API contained 89 posts when checked; all buyer-authored posts were checked and no later buyer update was present. A similar Make post uses the same handle: treated as one lead, not two buyers.
prospects.why_fit: A bounded repair can use our API, JavaScript and debugging work. Proposed price: $125 for one reproduced issue, test evidence and a short handover; confirm feasibility first.
prospects.why_now: Two-day-old explicit paid request. Strong urgency signal, but heavy competition and no fresh buyer response.
prospects.source_type: Original buyer post and public topic API
prospects.suggested_channel: User-authored n8n Community reply or invited DM. n8n prohibits copying AI output directly into threads; research notes are for preparation only.
prospects.opener: Internal preparation notes, not text to paste: ask whether the repair is still available; describe your actual relevant experience; establish the apps and failure; propose $125 only for a bounded, reproducible defect; confirm PayPal and AI-assisted implementation. Write your own reply after reading the post.
prospects.caution: Availability, exact requirements, AI assistance and PayPal payment must be agreed. The forum being open does not establish that the buyer is still hiring. Do not promise a fix before seeing the failure.

prospects.name: Carlos_Gomez1 — WhatsApp to Google Sheets
prospects.pain_signal: Posted in Make's Hire Help category on 14 September requesting a WhatsApp Cloud API and Google Sheets connection.
prospects.evidence: Original post identifies the two services. Other respondents quote prices, but those are competing offers, not the buyer's approved budget. The source does not specify incoming vs outgoing messages.
prospects.why_fit: Propose $125 for one inbound text-message flow if Meta and Make accounts are already ready: map fields, prevent duplicates, test output and document handover.
prospects.why_now: Six-day-old specific integration request; no verified hiring decision or budget.
prospects.source_title: I need help with a scenario to connect the WhatsApp Cloud API with Google Sheets
prospects.suggested_channel: User-authored reply in Make Hire Help. Make guidelines prohibit AI-generated responses; do not paste an assistant draft.
prospects.opener: Internal preparation notes, not text to paste: ask whether hiring remains open, incoming vs outgoing messages, whether the Meta number is active, budget and deadline. A one-direction inbound flow could be proposed at $125 after review. The user must author the Make response independently.
prospects.caution: PayPal, budget and availability unconfirmed. Account approval, outbound templates, historical imports and a second direction are outside the proposed small scope. Do not use another applicant's price as evidence of a funded budget.

prospects.name: OSQUARED — automation work in Porto
prospects.pain_signal: Porto company posted an automation contract on 16 September covering finance, contracts, sales and site workflows.
prospects.evidence: Buyer requests Portugal-based availability, production automation evidence and 2–3 weeks initially on site. Compensation is hourly or per phase, to be negotiated. Public business application address: office@osquared.pt.
prospects.why_fit: Portugal is a geographic match. Ask whether a separately paid, small workflow diagnostic is useful before a larger engagement. Proposed $250 diagnostic is our offer, not their advertised budget.
prospects.why_now: Recent local hiring signal, but the requested engagement is much larger than a one-week cash task.
prospects.source_title: Automation and Business Systems Lead — Real Estate Developer, Porto
prospects.suggested_channel: Employer's published business application email, with a truthful CV and portfolio; user sends.
prospects.opener: Hello, I saw your Porto automation role and am based in Portugal. My relevant project is CoWork OS: https://github.com/CoWork-OS/CoWork-OS. Would you consider a separately scoped $250 first milestone mapping one workflow, documenting its failure points and producing an implementation plan? I would confirm the scope and delivery date before committing. Please let me know whether that fits your process and whether PayPal payment on delivery is possible.
prospects.caution: Do not claim production n8n/Make credentials, on-site availability or case studies that are not true. Hiring timeline and PayPal are unknown; exclude from the one-week income forecast.

patterns.title: Small scope can shorten delivery
patterns.insight: The first two requests can potentially be reduced to one repair or integration direction, after reviewing the actual setup.

patterns.title: Payment is not yet confirmed
patterns.insight: All buyers need to agree a price, PayPal and acceptance/payment timing. None is guaranteed income.

patterns.title: Existing portfolio beats an invented case study
patterns.insight: Use relevant CoWork code and explain our actual contribution. Do not claim previous client results or platform certifications.

outreach_plan.first_step: Day 1: user reads the original requests and writes their own message to Dorian and Carlos, following each community's rules. The packet contains internal scoping notes, plus a general offer for suitable existing professional contacts. We prepare implementation from actual buyer replies.
outreach_plan.follow_up: Days 2–3: one polite follow-up if appropriate, then focus on responsive buyers. Confirm a sanitized reproducer, exact deliverable, acceptance test, AI permission, price and PayPal deadline. Days 3–6: implement, test, deliver and invoice each accepted job.
outreach_plan.success: By 27 September: at least $200 actually available after payment fees. $250 gross is a planning buffer, not a guarantee of net income. Deposits for undelivered work and pending payments do not count as earned cash. Day 7: verify settled payment, not just an invoice or accepted PR.

limits: All prospects are potential customers based on public signals, not confirmed buyers. Scores measure outreach fit, not probability of winning or being paid.
The user resides in Portugal, has no existing freelance/testing/bounty accounts, and reports that recent PayPal commercial payments were available without a hold. Future payments can still be held.
No outreach, account registration, proposal submission or security testing has been performed. No money has been earned or received.
Dorian's n8n and Make requests were deduplicated. Make API access returned 403; the public page was used, so later unseen replies may change status.
Discarded Bridge Builders $150–$250 trial: buyer said the role was filled. Older n8n posts were not treated as fresh merely because applicants bumped them.
Rami's RFQ prototype remains a scoping-stage backup, not commissioned work. NUBO's recent paid project opportunity requires fluent Spanish; eligibility is unknown.
Use the payment email privately after agreeing a job. Quotes are before any applicable taxes; do not publish sensitive payment or account details in a public service post.

Posting rules checked: Make bans AI-generated responses (https://community.make.com/guidelines). n8n prohibits copying AI output directly and requires personal understanding (https://community.n8n.io/t/this-forum-is-for-humans-by-humans/305091). The user should independently author community replies; this does not establish a ban on client-approved AI-assisted coding.
